question: Song (2025) chapter 7 (Tables 7.1-7.8) gives the evidence for Toda-Truku, Toda and Truku as changes of Proto-Toda-Truku, Proto-Toda and Proto-Truku. How are they entered, the subgroups being groups without proto-languages (decision song-seediq)?
chosen_reading: On each dialect, against Song's Proto-Seediq (system Song), beside the rows of Tables 4.3-4.23. New rows: *ə > i before y, > u before w, and full assimilation to a following vowel (Tables 7.1-7.2, with 4.22-4.23) for Central Toda and the two Truku dialects; initial *gə- > u- for Central and Eastern Toda (Table 7.5), and *ə > u next to *g elsewhere as sporadic; the sporadic changes of Table 7.3 (Central Toda, Central and Eastern Truku) and of Table 7.8 (Truku), each with its etymon in lexical_scope. Eastern Toda gets only the rows for which Song prints an Eastern Toda form (he has little data, pp. 155-156). Not entered: Table 7.5's *g > w, Table 7.6's *c > s and Table 7.7's *t, *d > c, ɟ before *i (already in from Tables 4.4, 4.8, 4.9, 4.13); the loss of *rə- in *rəsənaw > sənaw; Truku *aw > u after a coronal (*sawni > suni), because the diphthongs are not entered (song-seediq); Central Truku gisak from *gəsak; the lexical innovations of Tables 7.4, 7.9, 7.10.
alternatives: Make Toda-Truku, Toda and Truku proto-languages (Song writes PTo-TR and PTR forms) and state these changes once on each.
